subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: The Grapes of Wrath and Migrant Poverty
description: A quick, practical guide to The Grapes of Wrath and Migrant Poverty.

hook.text: John Steinbeck traveled with migrant workers in California and was horrified by what he witnessed.

buildup.text: The Grapes of Wrath followed the Joad family fleeing the Dust Bowl for the broken promise of California.

discovery.text: Published in 1939, the novel sold over four hundred thousand copies in its first year alone.

twist.text: California landowners publicly burned copies and accused Steinbeck of communist propaganda.

climax.text: The novel led Congress to investigate migrant conditions and prompted federal aid to farm workers.

punchline.text: A novel burned by the powerful brought help to the powerless.

quiz.question: How did California landowners react to The Grapes of Wrath?
options: They publicly burned copies and called it propaganda
They hired Steinbeck as a consultant
